title: The Deadliest Cat on Earth Weighs Less Than a House Cat

scenes.text: The deadliest cat on Earth fits in your two hands.
Not the lion. A lion hunting alone succeeds about one time in five.
This one succeeds six times in ten. The black-footed cat of southern Africa. Two to five pounds. Eight inches tall.
In one night it kills ten to fourteen rodents and small birds. One kill every fifty minutes, all night long.
One male caught twelve rodents in three and a half hours. In a single night it takes more prey than a leopard does in six months.
Two hundred times lighter than a lion. Three times deadlier. Still want to hold it?

description:
The deadliest cat on Earth is the black-footed cat of southern Africa, which weighs 2 to 5 pounds and lands a kill in about 60 percent of its hunts.
A lion hunting alone succeeds about 20 percent of the time. The black-footed cat kills 10 to 14 rodents or small birds a night, roughly one every 50 minutes, and catches more prey in one night than a leopard does in six months. Guinness World Records lists it as the most successful feline predator.
Which cat would you have guessed was the deadliest?
subject: black-footed cat
first_comment: It lives in Botswana, Namibia and South Africa and is listed as vulnerable. Which big cat did you think was the best hunter before this?
